title: Mince Pies
subtitle: Traditional British Christmas mince pies with buttery shortcrust pastry
excerpt: Crisp, buttery shortcrust pastry cases filled with spiced fruit mincemeat and topped with a pastry lid or star. The essential Christmas bake.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mince pies have been made in Britain since the medieval period, when they genuinely contained minced meat mixed with dried fruit, spices, and fat as a way of preserving meat. The meat was gradually reduced over centuries as sugar became cheaper, and by the Victorian era the filling had become entirely fruit-based. The name mincemeat (and the pie itself) is derived from this earlier meat-containing version. Mince pies were associated with Christmas from at least the sixteenth century and their preparation was banned under Oliver Cromwell's Puritan government in the 1650s as an example of Popish excess, which only increased their popularity when the ban was lifted. Good mincemeat can be bought ready-made; homemade mincemeat made with suet, dried fruit, apple, brandy, and spices is better but requires making several weeks ahead.

recipeTools.notes: A 12-hole tart or mince pie tin.

content.text: Keep the pastry cold at every stage: this is what keeps it short and crumbly. If the kitchen is warm, chill the pastry between each stage. Do not overfill the cases: the mincemeat expands as it heats and will bubble over the edges if the cases are too full. A heaped teaspoon per case is enough. Dust with icing sugar while still warm.

items.preparation: for the pastry, plus extra to dust

content.text: Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk, salt, and 2 tablespoons of cold water. Bring together into a dough. Wrap in cling film and chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Roll out two-thirds of the pastry on a lightly floured surface to 3 mm thick. Stamp out 12 rounds large enough to line the holes of a 12-hole tart tin. Press gently in. Fill each case with a heaped teaspoon of mincemeat.

Roll out the remaining pastry and cut out lids or stars. Place over each pie. Pinch or press the edges to seal. Brush with a little milk or beaten egg. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until pale golden. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then lift out. Dust with icing sugar while still warm. Serve warm or at room temperature.
